Her bold act of chaining herself to protest against the bars' ban on women sparked vital changes in public policy. Alongside challenging the unjust marriage bar, her relentless advocacy has left a lasting legacy. A recently unveiled bronze statue in Brisbane commemorates her monumental contributions, symbolizing the ongoing fight for equality and the empowerment of women across Australia.

articles.title: 16th-century book of 'blood rain', five suns sold for £100k may now fetch £1m
articles.summary: An illustrated manuscript known as the Book of Miracles documents extraordinary natural events from the 16th century. It features 167 paintings showcasing phenomena perceived as divine warnings, including blood rain and comets. The manuscript, discovered in a German castle, is the only known surviving copy of its kind. A December auction will allow public institutions to acquire the rare volume for the first time.

articles.title: Mumbai teen raises Rs 22 lakh for 560-pupil Dharavi school, seeks Rs 1.5 crore
articles.summary: Daniel Gupta, a college student, is working to secure a permanent home for New Life School in Dharavi. He has already raised Rs 22 lakh but aims to reach Rs 1.5 crore to stabilize its future. The school, which serves around 560 children, has operated without owning its premises for nearly four decades. Through the initiative Dharavi Rising, Daniel seeks to highlight educational needs in the community.

articles.title: 'Who ordered SIR?' Cong seeks SC nod to pose 48 questions to EC over 'vote chori'

articles.title: Jay Shah reappointed as ICC Chair; BCCI hails leadership ahead of cricket's Oly return
articles.summary: In a unanimous decision, Jay Shah has been reappointed as ICC Chair for a second term at the helm of world cricket. His new tenure will coincide with cricket's return to the Olympics at Los Angeles 2028. The BCCI hailed his contributions to the game, including the landmark launch of the Women's Premier League. Shah's second term comes at a crucial time as cricket looks to expand its footprint in emerging markets and reach wider audiences across the world.

articles.title: Europe's migrant crackdown: Rejected asylum seekers face deportation to Rwanda
articles.summary: Five EU countries, including Germany and Denmark, are planning to set up a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda. This centre will specifically handle rejected asylum seekers who have exhausted all legal options to remain in Europe. The countries aim to make this facility operational by 2027 and will initially accommodate around 100 migrants. The proposed arrangement reflects a broader shift in the EU’s immigration policy and deportation strategies.

articles.title: India joins US-led alliance to secure AI supply chains amid China tech rivalry
articles.summary: India has taken a significant step by joining a US-led initiative alongside nine other nations to secure their artificial intelligence supply chains. This coalition is designed to protect sensitive technologies while countering competition from China. By creating working groups focused on cooperation in AI policy and security, these countries aim to fortify their economic and national security, building on last year's Pax Silica program that addresses critical resource safeguarding.

Inspired by her journey, Boyd founded two charities focused on assisting young mothers and children with disabilities, underscoring the vital importance of rigorous medical standards during childbirth.

articles.title: Redrawing Pak: Ministers back 12-province plan but pol, constitutional hurdles remain

Senior officials argue that smaller provinces could enhance public service delivery. Yet, this ambitious initiative faces political hurdles and requires unity among major parties. Redefining boundaries will necessitate constitutional amendments, and a potential referendum may follow, pending parliamentary consent.

articles.title: Minnesota man jumps onto moving school bus, saves 19 children

He quickly jumped aboard and halted the vehicle, safeguarding 19 young lives. The driver was promptly taken to the hospital and is recovering well. For his bravery, Ahmed was honored with accolades, including a dedicated day in St. Paul.

articles.title: Scientist builds first dictionary of zebra finch calls after a decade
articles.summary: Dr. Julie Elie has meticulously created an acoustic dictionary showcasing zebra finch calls, categorizing 11 distinct vocalization types. Her groundbreaking research suggests that these birds actively comprehend the meanings of their calls, indicating that zebra finches employ a nuanced communication method. This could revolutionize human perspectives on interspecies dialogue, promoting reciprocal understanding. Nevertheless, fully unraveling avian communication remains a complex, ongoing research endeavor for many scientists.

articles.title: Google CEO congratulates SpaceX; says 'still feels like science fiction '

Despite the success, a first-stage booster explosion occurred shortly after liftoff during the tests.
